_about: The agent interfaces, one entry each, and their status. tools/readme/make-readme.py writes the README section from this file and site/build.py checks the landing page against it.

status is one of Built, Written, Designed. Built: the code is on main and every path in tests exists there (CI runs them on every change). Written: the document named in link exists. Designed: decided, not yet in the tree.
Both scripts refuse a Built entry with no tests or a missing test path, and a Built or Written entry whose link is missing.
build lists the items of the agent build list (A1 to A9) the entry covers.

interfaces.name: MCP server
interfaces.lets_you: connect an AI assistant to a running runner over MCP (Model Context Protocol, the common way an assistant calls a program's tools): it can read tracks and quality marks and propose changes, with the authority of the person it acts for and no more

interfaces.name: Agent as a source
interfaces.lets_you: have an agent publish tracks or notes on the goat fabric (the network the runner reads and publishes on) under its own name, marked as agent-derived with its model and inputs; the processors take them in like any other source

interfaces.name: Agent as an adjudicator
interfaces.lets_you: let an agent or an analyst settle a hard case with a hint ("treat A and B as one object", "keep A and B apart") that the engines record and trace like any other input, so a replay stays exact

interfaces.name: Settings proposals and site auto-approval
interfaces.lets_you: have an agent propose a pack or config change that a person approves, or that a site rule approves within set bounds once the benchmark passes; every change is logged and can be reverted in one step

interfaces.name: Audit log
interfaces.lets_you: see every agent call and action afterwards: who it acted for, which tool, a fingerprint (hash) of its inputs, and the result

interfaces.name: The "why?" explainer
interfaces.lets_you: ask in plain words why two tracks were joined or kept apart, and get an answer in which every sentence cites the trace record it comes from

interfaces.name: Build-your-own guide
interfaces.lets_you: build your own integration from one runnable example per interface (MCP, source, adjudicator, settings), each run in CI
